text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Government to reshuffle organisation of local authorities and administrations to improve development of towns and rural areas.
-- Tax council calls for a reform of corporate tax system including a shift to a unique tax nationwide, weighted by criteria of local wealth and population.
-- Rise of the dollar gives breathing space to French industrialists, who expect a growth of their activity.
-- CFDT union at Aerospatiale criticises government's order of 48 Rafale aircraft to Dassault and consider it as a "gift".
-- Spanish government supports a partially state-owned Spanish digital-TV bouquet, starts legal action to counter rival offer by Canal Plus and Prisa.
-- Credit National seeks investigation by bourse watchdog COB over equity transactions.
-- Employers and unions in transports sector to meet tomorrow with minister over shorter work hours and early retirement.
-- Government considers a multi-annual order of 140 to 184 Leclerc tanks to Giat Industries for an estimated total of up to five billion francs.
-- CGIP chairman Ernest-Antoine Seilliere calls for a quick decision of its German partners on whether to increase their stake in Cap Gemini.
-- Aluminium prices expected to keep rising.
-- Canal Plus chairman Pierre Lescure says Nethold merger will no longer weigh on accounts from 1999, expects 1996 profits slightly higher than in 1995.
-- Investigators to look into alleged bribery involved in sale of Paris headquarters of firms including Pechiney .
